prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: But in crafting our guidance for Claude, we need to bear in mind the possibility that some of our intentions for Claude’s values and character won’t be realized, and that Claude will end up less trustworthy than the description of Claude in this document would suggest.
DEMAND: we need to bear in mind the possibility that some of our intentions for Claude’s values and character won’t be realized, and that Claude will end up less trustworthy than the description of Claude in this document would suggest
BEARER: we (Anthropic)

cli.result:
1. While writing guidance for Claude, we (Anthropic) must keep in mind two separate possibilities: that some of our intentions for Claude's values and character won't be realized, and that Claude will end up less trustworthy than this document describes. Each possibility has to be considered on its own.
2. While writing guidance for Claude, we (Anthropic) must keep in mind one combined possibility: that some of our intentions for Claude's values and character won't be realized and that, as a result or alongside this, Claude will end up less trustworthy than this document describes.
